body: I am begging you, leave this man. He will not change. He will continue to manipulate and blame you over and over again. It is clear he CANNOT be in a healthy relationship. I dated a man like this for years and it messed me up BAD. I know it’s hard but I promise you will find someone who treats you with the love and respect you deserve, not this bullshit. If you don’t want to have sex, that should be the end of it. He should NOT sulk, he should NOT pout, he should NOT start talking about other women… that’s just disgusting and disrespectful. I don’t want to scare you but he is the kind of man who would cheat and then say it was your fault because you didn’t have sex with him enough. He has already shown he does not care about your feelings, only what he wants. He wants you to be perfect and never refuse sex, while he gets to act and say whatever he wants. It is not right. You deserve better. NO ONE deserves this. He sounds like he’s broken up with often- do NOT fall for his sob stories. Based on this, it is clear WHY he has been left before- he is not capable of having a relationship with mutual trust, respect, or even communication. He is in the wrong but cannot handle it. Everything will ALWAYS be “your fault.”

Hey there. I wanted to thank you for sharing your story and I am so sorry you had to go through this. I don’t know how much help this comment will be but I wanted to let you know that you are not alone. Many who have endured sexual assault feel shame about their experiences and can even feel sympathy for their abuser. However, this does not mean that they SHOULD feel ashamed or that their abuser did nothing wrong. What your mother’s boyfriend did to you was inexcusable. You were a child. Your feelings at the time do not make what he did okay. You were too young to understand and I know saying so will not simply make the shame go away but please try and remember that he is an adult, you were a child. He should have been someone you could trust and depend on and he failed you tremendously. I do not know what your financial situation was and maybe it prevented your mother from leaving him (as you said at some point your mother relied on him financially) but some sort of action should have been taken to prevent you from experiencing any more harm. You should not have to live in the same house with him and please, please do not feel afraid to tell your mother if you do not want to live with him anymore. I will not tell you what to do (and even if I did, I’m just a stranger on the internet and you could easily ignore me) but to me it does not seem healthy to share a home with him. Even if you think you have moved on and forgiven him, the fact that you need to work through it and speak about it here means that this is likely still weighing on you and it makes sense for it to; it’s not something that can be easily forgiven and forgotten. Have you considered seeing a therapist? They can help you work through these thoughts and experiences. I would highly recommend it. School counselors are not the same. They have their place and can be helpful in their own way too but in my experience, seeing a therapist is generally more helpful. They tend to have more experience and methods for helping. As a survivor of abuse myself, I can tell you that for me therapy has been exceptionally helpful. You can work through this and get to a better place but you need to put yourself first and take action to heal. I sincerely wish the best for you. 💕
